title: Rosalind and the Wolf
premise: Hazel Oyelaran, a runaway apprentice turned smuggler's guide, is hired to escort a mute child who speaks a language older than any living kingdom — the tongue of Thornfell itself, a country erased from maps and memory three centuries ago. The child's words are slowly unmaking the borders that buried Thornfell, and the Crown's inquisitors, the smugglers' own guild, and the ghost-remnant of Thornfell's last queen all want the child for their own ends. Hazel, guided by Rosalind, the hedge-witch she abandoned, must choose between selling the child to buy her own pardon or carrying them through the dying mountain roads to the Door — the one threshold out of a country that officially never existed. In the end Hazel opens the Door at terrible cost, sending the child home while Rosalind stays behind as the new keeper of Thornfell's memory, and Hazel walks out of the mountains changed: no longer running, but carrying justice that no law will ever name.
about_author: Ivo Fairweather is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping borderlands that appear on no official survey, an obsession that seeps into every page of their fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable weather, unreliable neighbors, and excellent tea.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She guides contraband through the Thornfell passes, calculating risk like currency, and refuses a letter from her old mistress Rosalind without opening it. Establishes her transactional worldview and the wound beneath it. Beat: guarded competence masking guilt.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Wrong Hour
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A child appears at her waystation door during a storm, barefoot, unafraid, speaking a language no scholar would recognize. Hazel recognizes one word anyway — from Rosalind's lessons she pretended to forget. Beat: unease and reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: What the Guild Pays For Silence
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The smugglers' guild offers Hazel a fortune to deliver the child to a buyer in Lowmark. She haggles, accepts, tells herself it's just another job. Beat: self-deception dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Language That Predates Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Child's POV (rendered through sensation and image). The child, Wren, remembers a country that was unwritten — its fields, its Door, its erasure. First hint that Wren's speech physically alters the world around them. Beat: elegiac loss.

chapters.title: Rosalind's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Flashback, Hazel's POV. Years earlier, Rosalind taught that names are load-bearing; Hazel called it superstition and left. The flashback mirrors her present choice to sell Wren. Beat: the past sharpening into accusation.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Vane Descends
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. A Crown inquisitor arrives in the foothills hunting 'unlicensed speech,' burning a village archive as a warning. Vane believes erasure is mercy. Beat: cold ideological menace introduced.

chapters.title: The Road Through Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On the road, Wren hums and dead orchards blossom out of season; guild scouts see it and whisper. Hazel realizes the cargo is not cargo. Beat: dawning responsibility.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A guild contact demands a higher price upon seeing Wren work small wonders. Hazel pays with her mother's ring — the last thing she owns that isn't owed. Beat: sacrifice she doesn't yet understand.

chapters.title: The Queen Who Was Never Crowned
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. In a hollow beneath the mountains, the remnant of Thornfell's last queen stirs, drawn by Wren's voice. She wants her country back, whatever it costs the living. Beat: tragic antagonist revealed.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Hazel and Wren's shared POV, alternating. Trapped by a whiteout in a shepherd's hut, they build a fragile vocabulary together — Hazel teaching trade-tongue, learning fragments of the old speech. Beat: found family begins.

chapters.title: What Vane Burns
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane interrogates the guild, learns Hazel's route, and executes a smuggler for knowing too much. We see Vane's genuine conviction: order as kindness. Beat: the enemy made human and more frightening.

chapters.title: Lowmark's Gilded Cage
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Arrival in Lowmark; the buyer is a collector of extinct things who keeps Wren in a soundproofed room. Hazel takes her payment and cannot sleep. Beat: complicity curdling.

chapters.title: The Word on the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. From inside the collector's vault, Wren speaks to the lock in the old tongue — not to escape, but to ask it politely. It opens. Beat: quiet awe; power as courtesy, not force.

chapters.title: Running Again
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel finds Wren gone from the vault and faces a choice: report the escape for reward or flee with the child. She runs — and this time she knows exactly what she's running toward. Beat: first true moral choice made.

chapters.title: The Guild Declares Debt
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvo's POV. The guild marks Hazel for collection; her debts are sold to Vane's office. Betrayal becomes policy. Beat: the lawless world proving as merciless as the lawful one.

chapters.title: Letters Unopened
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Cornered, Hazel finally reads Rosalind's letters — all of them, years' worth. Rosalind knew about Thornfell, about children like Wren, and wrote asking only that Hazel come home. Beat: grief and shame breaking open.

chapters.title: The Hedge at World's Edge
chapters.summary: Hazel and Wren's POV. They reach Rosalind's cottage; the reunion is awkward, unforgiven, practical. Rosalind examines Wren and goes pale: the child is a Door-key, and the Door is closing. Beat: reconciliation begun, not completed.

chapters.title: Three Teachers
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind, Hazel, and Wren study together — witchcraft, smuggling-craft, and the old tongue braided into one plan. For one chapter, they are simply a household. Beat: warmth before the fall.

chapters.title: Vane at the Hedge
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane raids the cottage; Rosalind buys their escape with a working that unmakes her garden and half her memory. Hazel drags Wren into the deep passes alone. Beat: cost made flesh; guilt rekindled.

chapters.title: The Passes Turn Against Them
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The mountains themselves begin forgetting the smuggler's roads — Wren's growing power erasing even paths. Hazel's greatest expertise becomes useless. Beat: helplessness of the competent.

chapters.title: The Queen's Offer
chapters.summary: Queen's POV. The queen's remnant reaches Hazel through dreams, offering to restore everything Hazel has lost — Rosalind's memory, her name cleared — if Wren is brought to her instead of the Door. Beat: temptation with a truthful face.

chapters.title: Wren Asks the Question
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, now verbal in trade-tongue, asks Hazel what 'home' means when your country is a grave. Hazel lies badly, then tells the truth. Beat: the emotional core of the book.

chapters.title: Corvo's Ambush
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The guild corners them at Sorrow Bridge; Hazel spends every trick she knows and wins free only by collapsing the bridge behind them, stranding herself and Wren on the forgotten side. Beat: no way back but forward.

chapters.title: The Country That Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Beyond the bridge lies Thornfell as it was — a preserved echo where the erased dead live their last day on loop. Wren is recognized; Hazel is a stranger here. Beat: haunting beauty, uncanny grief.

chapters.title: The Last Day, Again
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. They walk through Thornfell's eternal final evening: a wedding that always ends, a baker who never finishes his loaves. Hazel sees what erasure really means. Beat: horror transmuted into compassion.

chapters.title: The Queen in Her Ruin
chapters.summary: Queen's POV. Face to face, the queen makes her case: Wren can resurrect Thornfell whole, at the price of the borderlands' living thousands. She is not wrong about her grief — only about her arithmetic. Beat: antagonist fully sympathetic, still refused.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel refuses the queen, articulating the book's thesis: you cannot pay for one country's life with another's death. The queen's sorrow turns to wrath. Beat: moral spine stated under maximum pressure.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Echo
chapters.summary: Hazel and Wren's POV. Hunted through the echoing country by the queen's dead, saved by its ordinary people — the looping dead choosing, once, to break their loop. Beat: solidarity of the forgotten.

chapters.title: Rosalind Returns
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Half-remembering, Rosalind followed the unmade roads and finds them at the Door's threshold. She and Hazel fight back-to-back against Vane's vanguard. Beat: reconciliation completed in action, not words.

chapters.title: Vane's Crisis
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Inside Thornfell's echo, Vane confronts proof that the erased were people, not errors. Vane's certainty cracks; some soldiers defect, Vane does not — but hesitates. Beat: enemy shaken, tragedy locked in.

chapters.title: The Door Is Closing
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the Door, Wren falters: opening it means going home alone, and home may no longer want them. Hazel gives the speech she needed someone to give her at fifteen. Beat: mentorship reversed into grace.

chapters.title: The Queen's Last March
chapters.summary: Queen's POV. The queen commits her remnant to seizing the Door rather than let Thornfell stay dead. Even her own echo-people waver. Beat: antagonist's point of no return.

chapters.title: Battle of the Threshold
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The climactic battle at the Door: guild, Crown, echoes, and witches collide. Rosalind holds the ward-line; Corvo falls to his own greed; Vane and Hazel face each other across the threshold stone. Beat: chaos with clear stakes.

chapters.title: The Word That Opens
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren speaks the Door open — not with force but with the old tongue's word for 'guest.' The Door accepts Wren, and, unexpectedly, offers passage to all the echoes. Beat: climax resolved by mercy, not violence.

chapters.title: Vane's Choice
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Offered entry to a country Vane spent a career denying, Vane stands down — ordering troops to withdraw, then walking into the mountains alone, sentence unfinished. Beat: ambiguous redemption, earned ambiguity.

chapters.title: The Queen Stays
chapters.summary: Queen's POV. The queen could pass through and live again elsewhere; instead she chooses to remain as her country's keeper, asking Rosalind — not commanding — to remember with her. Beat: antagonist's arc lands in dignity.

chapters.title: What Hazel Carries Out
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The Door closes. Hazel descends with Rosalind, carrying Wren's parting gift: fluency in the old tongue, and the duty of a witness. Beat: quiet devastation and purpose.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In the lowlands, Hazel testifies nowhere, files nothing — instead she opens the waystations as a network that hides the hunted and teaches the forbidden alphabet. Justice as infrastructure. Beat: theme embodied.

chapters.title: The Keeper and the Guide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Hazel and Rosalind. A year later: Rosalind tends the Door's outer side, Hazel runs the roads above it, and a second child arrives at a waystation door, speaking a language that predates kingdoms. Beat: cyclical hope.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, coda. Rosalind explains the title's old story: the wolf was never the danger; the danger was the country that named it so. Hazel, once the runaway, now the one who waits up with the lamp, lets the next traveler in. Beat: resolution, transformation, welcome.
